title: Serif or sans-serif? Typography basics
examples: What is the difference between serif and sans-serif?
How many fonts should a poster have?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Choose the font that fits the job

explain.say: Look at any poster, book or phone screen. The letters themselves are designed, and the way they look changes how the words feel. That art is called typography. Look at the board: two big families of letters, serif and sans-serif.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Choose the font that fits the job

explain.say: Look at the serif side. Serifs are the tiny feet and flicks at the ends of letters, like in Times New Roman or Georgia. They feel classic and formal, and many printed books use them. Can you spot serifs in a newspaper headline?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Choose the font that fits the job

explain.say: Now the sans-serif side. Sans is the French word for without, so sans-serif means without feet: clean, simple strokes, like Arial or Helvetica. These are easy to read on screens and road signs. Which family is this lesson's text in?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Choose the font that fits the job

explain.say: Size matters too. Look at the board: a big heading, a smaller subheading, body text, and a tiny caption. This order of sizes is called visual hierarchy, and it tells your eyes what to read first. Which would you read first?

Brilliant! Here is a designer's checklist for your next poster. Look at the board and tick it off. Wow fact: printing with movable type began with Bi Sheng in China around 1040, centuries before Gutenberg's press in Germany around 1450. Challenge: redesign a poster using just two fonts.

faq.a: A serif is a small line or foot at the end of the strokes of a letter. Fonts with them, like Times New Roman, are called serif fonts.
asks: What are the feet on letters called?
Is Times New Roman a serif font?

faq.a: Sans is French for without, so sans-serif fonts have no serifs, just clean strokes. Arial, Helvetica and Lexend are sans-serif fonts.
asks: What is the difference between serif and sans-serif?

faq.a: Visual hierarchy is arranging text and images by size, weight and position so people see the most important thing first, then the next.
asks: How do designers guide your eyes?

faq.q: How many fonts should a poster have?
faq.a: Usually no more than two: one for headings and one for body text. Too many fonts look messy and are harder to read.
asks: Can I use lots of fonts?
How do I choose fonts for a poster?

faq.a: Typography is the art of choosing and arranging letters: the fonts, sizes, spacing and layout, so text is clear to read and feels right.

facts: Bi Sheng invented movable type printing in China around 1040, using clay characters.
Johannes Gutenberg developed his movable metal type printing press in Mainz, Germany, around 1450.

quiz.why: Arial has no serifs, just clean strokes.

wrong.1: Times New Roman has serifs, the little feet.
wrong.2: Georgia is a serif font too.

quiz.say: On a poster, what should usually be the biggest text?
quiz.show: The biggest text on a poster is…
quiz.why: Visual hierarchy makes the most important words, the heading, biggest.

wrong.1: Small print is least important, so it is smallest.
wrong.2: A page number is minor information.
